# A cap-band quadrilateral whose canonical bridge triangle leaves the band

This is an exact obstruction to automatically removing the initial cap-ceiling hypothesis from the finite corner-loss barrier. It does not contradict the ordinary row inequalities or OC.

Let

    T=conv{(1,0),(-4/9,1),(-4/9,-1)},
    v_1=(1,0), v_2=(-1/2,26/45), v_3=(-1/2,-26/45),
    K=T intersect {x<=2/3}.

The three normals span the plane, sum to zero, and their source zero is interior to both bodies. The quadrilateral vertices are (-4/9,-1),(2/3,-3/13),(2/3,3/13),(-4/9,1).

The triangle has total area 13/9. Its raw cap areas for v_i dot w>=0 are respectively 9/13,8/13,8/13. Thus its cap fractions are

    (81/169,72/169,72/169).

In particular its first fraction exceeds 128/279, with exact difference 967/47151.

The six ray endpoints are

    x=0:                (0,9/13),(0,-9/13),
    v_2 dot w=0:        (4/9,5/13),(-4/9,-5/13),
    v_3 dot w=0:        (4/9,-5/13),(-4/9,5/13).

All have x<=4/9<2/3. Consequently truncation leaves the three full sections and all six ray endpoints unchanged. The removed tip lies strictly in the unique region of cap 1 and has area 1/13. It follows that

    |K|=160/117,
    Q_1(K)=Q_2(K)=Q_3(K)=8/13,
    q_1(K)=q_2(K)=q_3(K)=9/20<128/279.

The three lines joining the endpoint pairs that bound the double sectors are the original three edge lines of T. Hence their bounded canonical bridge triangle really is T; there is no change of the reference triangle hidden in the comparison.

For calibration, K obeys all three ordinary Lorentz rows. Its normalized section factors are

    sigma_1=18/13, sigma_2=sigma_3=20/13,
    M=sum Q_i/sigma_i=56/45.

Thus the row data are

    f_1=10sqrt(5)/21, f_2=f_3=3sqrt(5)/7.

The first row equals 10sqrt(5)/21+45/49<195/98<2, using sqrt(5)<9/4. Each other row equals 3sqrt(5)/7+1805/1764<1753/882<2. The example therefore identifies only a genuine missing hypothesis in that particular transfer theorem.

## The full sorted profile does not repair the implication

There is a second entirely rational example which also obeys the stricter sorted cap profile. Put

    T'=conv{(1,0),(-9/20,1),(-9/20,-1)},
    v'_1=(1,0), v'_2=(-1/2,261/440), v'_3=(-1/2,-261/440),
    K'=T' intersect {x<=37/50}.

The triangle has area 29/20 and cap fractions (400/841,360/841,360/841). Its first fraction exceeds 128/279 by 3952/234639. The two endpoints surrounding its unique first corner have x=9/20, and the other four endpoints have x=0 or -9/20. Thus all three sections survive the truncation unchanged. In particular the canonical double-bridge triangle of K' is T'.

The removed tip area is 169/3625, and direct subtraction gives

    |K'|=20349/14500,
    (Q'_1,Q'_2,Q'_3)=(2331/3625,18/29,18/29),
    (q'_1,q'_2,q'_3)=(1036/2261,1000/2261,1000/2261).

Every cap lies in the required band:

    q'_min>20/49,
    128/279-q'_max=364/630819>0.

Moreover

    q'_min+q'_mid+q'_max/4=2259/2261<1,
    sum q'_i=3036/2261<125/93.

The first sorted-profile slack is exactly 2/2261. Hence neither that full profile nor the lower cap bound forces the canonical comparison triangle to satisfy the initial upper ceiling. An extension of the transfer argument needs additional information even on this rational quadrilateral family.
